feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence from earlier iterations: iteration 3 (y=0.08, wheel_track 0.13, wheel_radius 0.04, mass 0.6, kp 4.0, kd 0.4) gave 16/20 oval and 7/20 s-bend completions, steering_oscillation about 0.30 to 0.31, and 0/20 slalom completions at max_error 0.064. Iteration 4 (mass 0.5, body_length 0.12, wheel_track 0.12, kp 3.8, kd 0.45) gave 20/20 oval and 17/20 s-bend completions, steering_oscillation 0.21 on the oval and 0.24 on the slalom, and slalom progress 0.43 with max_error 0.065. So the lighter body reduced oscillation while still improving completions, and the slalom failure is turn response on alternating bends rather than sensing or speed. Integration work: I kept the seven-sensor weights at x/0.015, kept ki 0.15 for the motor mismatch, and raised kd to 0.5 to damp the faster heading response. The next race decides the next change. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.32 on the s-bend or slalom, the agility gain has outrun the damping, so return wheel_track toward 0.12 m. If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 while oscillation stays at or below 0.32, the next lever is lower yaw inertia, not more track width. If oval or s-bend completions fall below iteration 4 levels, the lighter body has cost stability, so restore mass toward 0.5 kg.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 on the s-bend or slalom: set wheel_track back to 0.12 m, since iteration 4 at 0.12 m kept slalom oscillation at 0.24 and oval oscillation at 0.21, while iteration 2 at 0.11 m with kp 4.0 overshot to 0.27 to 0.28.

If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 while steering_oscillation stays at or below 0.32: try mass 0.4 kg with body_length 0.10 m, since iteration 4 moved slalom progress from 0.34 to 0.43 when yaw inertia fell and failure stayed at max_error 0.065.
If oval or s-bend completions drop below iteration 4's 20/20 and 17/20: return mass to 0.5 kg, since the 0.5 kg body in iteration 4 completed every oval run and 85% of s-bend runs.
